key_facts: Fire Point secured agreements from over a dozen European defense companies for the Freyja missile defense project.
Fire Point aims to achieve its first successful interception by mid-2027.
Fire Point aims to produce a ballistic interceptor for less than €1 million ($1.2 million) per missile, a quarter to a sixth the cost of a Patriot.
Norway's Kongsberg is working on the Freyja command center, and Germany's Diehl Defence is reportedly providing the guidance system.
Fire Point is building its own engine for its FP5 cruise missile (Flamingo) after running short of second-hand jet engines.
